subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: T cell and NK cell lymphomas: biology, histology and targeted systemic therapy

steps.tx: **Peripheral T-cell lymphomas** comprise a heterogeneous group of aggressive lymphoid malignancies arising from mature **post-thymic** T-lymphocytes or natural killer cells. Neoplastic T-cells characteristically express pan-T-cell differentiation markers including CD2, CD3, CD5, and CD7, though frequent loss of one or more antigen markers aids diagnostic confirmation. Clonal T-cell receptor beta or gamma gene rearrangements confirm monoclonality in challenging cases.

steps.tx: Systemic **Anaplastic large cell** lymphoma is pathologically divided into ALK-positive and ALK-negative subtypes based on expression of the anaplastic lymphoma kinase. ALK-positive disease is driven by the recurrent t(2;5)(p23;q35) translocation fusing nucleophosmin to ALK, producing the oncogenic **NPM1-ALK** chimeric protein. ALK-positive patients present at a younger age and experience significantly superior five-year survival compared to ALK-negative individuals.

steps.tx: Targeted antibody-drug conjugate therapy has transformed frontline management for CD30-expressing mature T-cell malignancies. In the landmark **ECHELON-2** trial, adding **Brentuximab vedotin** to cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, and **prednisone** significantly prolonged progression-free and overall survival compared to traditional CHOP. This established BV-CHP as the preferred global standard of care for CD30-positive peripheral T-cell lymphomas and anaplastic large cell lymphomas.

steps.tx: **Angioimmunoblastic T-cell** lymphoma represents a distinct entity derived from neoplastic **follicular helper T cells**. Typical clinical hallmarks include generalized lymphadenopathy, constitutional B symptoms, pruritic morbilliform cutaneous rashes, polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia, and autoimmune phenomena. Molecular sequencing uncovers recurrent somatic mutations in epigenetic and signaling genes including RHOA G17V, TET2, DNMT3A, and IDH2, providing biological rationale for hypomethylating agents.
steps.say: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma represents a distinct entity derived from neoplastic follicular helper T cells. Typical clinical hallmarks include generalized lymphadenopathy, B symptoms, morbilliform rashes, polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia, and autoimmune phenomena. Molecular sequencing uncovers recurrent somatic mutations in epigenetic regulators.

steps.tx: **Extranodal NK/T-cell** lymphoma, nasal type, is an aggressive, destructive malignancy predominantly localized to the midfacial upper aerodigestive tract. Pathogenesis is universally driven by clonal **Epstein-Barr virus** infection. Neoplastic cells express high levels of P-glycoprotein, causing intrinsic resistance to anthracyclines. Modern therapeutic regimens overcome multidrug resistance by incorporating L-**asparaginase** or pegaspargase alongside non-cross-resistant platinum agents and radiotherapy.

steps.tx: **Mycosis fungoides** represents the most prevalent primary cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, characterized by indolent evolution across cutaneous patches, indurated plaques, and eventual exophytic tumours. Histopathological examination demonstrates atypical epidermotropic T-lymphocytes lining the basal epidermis and forming intraepidermal clusters known as **Pautrier microabscesses**. Early patch-stage disease responds favourably to skin-directed therapies including topical corticosteroids, phototherapy, and localized radiation.

steps.tx: The section shows **mycosis fungoides**, the commonest primary **cutaneous lymphoma**, evolving from flat patches toward raised plaques. Atypical **cerebriform lymphocytes** crowd upward into the epidermis and gather into intraepidermal clusters called **Pautrier microabscesses**. Recognizing this epidermotropic pattern separates early disease that answers to skin directed care.
steps.say: Mycosis fungoides is the most frequent primary lymphoma of skin and moves slowly from patches to plaques and then tumours. Under the microscope, atypical cerebriform T lymphocytes enter the epidermis and form small clusters called Pautrier microabscesses. This view captures that hallmark. Early patch disease often responds well to skin directed treatment such as topical steroids or light therapy.

steps.tx: **Sezary syndrome** is the aggressive, leukemic variant of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma defined by a classic clinical triad: generalized pruritic erythroderma, diffuse peripheral lymphadenopathy, and circulating neoplastic T-lymphocytes. These circulating atypical mononuclear cells with highly folded, cerebriform nuclei are designated **Sezary cells**. Immunophenotypic flow cytometry demonstrates a characteristic CD4-predominant phenotype with frequent loss of CD7 and CD26 surface markers.
steps.say: Sezary syndrome is the aggressive, leukemic variant of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma defined by a classic clinical triad: generalized pruritic erythroderma, diffuse peripheral lymphadenopathy, and circulating neoplastic T-lymphocytes. These circulating atypical cells with highly folded cerebriform nuclei are designated Sezary cells. Immunophenotyping shows CD4 predominance with loss of CD7.

steps.tx: **Adult T-cell leukemia**-lymphoma is a distinct peripheral T-cell neoplasm etiologically caused by the human T-cell lymphotropic virus type 1 (**HTLV-1**). Endemic in southwestern Japan, the Caribbean basin, and parts of sub-Saharan Africa, acute ATLL presents aggressively with rapid-onset lymphocytosis, widespread lymphadenopathy, lytic bone lesions, and severe refractory hypercalcaemia. Antiviral therapy combining zidovudine and interferon-alpha produces clinical responses in leukemic subtypes.
steps.say: Adult T-cell leukemia-lymphoma is a distinct peripheral T-cell neoplasm etiologically caused by the human T-cell lymphotropic virus type 1 or HTLV-1. Acute ATLL presents aggressively with rapid-onset lymphocytosis, widespread lymphadenopathy, lytic bone lesions, and severe refractory hypercalcaemia. Antiviral therapy combining zidovudine and interferon-alpha produces clinical responses.
